items.title: How to Watch Out-of-Market NBA Games: Bypassing Blackouts With A VPN
items.summary: There is nothing quite as frustrating for a hardcore basketball fan as settling in on the couch, firing up NBA League Pass, and being hit with that dreaded message: "This game is blacked out in your area." Whether it is a local blackout protecting a regional sports network or a national blackout because the game is on ESPN or NBC, blackout restrictions are the bane of every die-hard fan's existence. You paid for League Pass to watch hoops, not to look at an error screen. READ MORE : Full List Of NBA Regional Sports Networks Fortunately, there is a reliable workaround to regain control of your viewing experience: using a Virtual Private Network (VPN). By changing your device's digital location, you can bypass these geo-restrictions and stream the games you want. Here is the complete RealGM guide on how to use a VPN to watch any out-of-market NBA game this season. The Problem: Why Are NBA Games Blacked Out? Before fixing the issue, it helps to understand it. The NBA uses your IP address to determine your physical location. Local Blackouts: If you live in the broadcast territory of the teams playing, League Pass will block you from watching the game live to force you to watch it on the local Regional Sports Network (RSN). National Blackouts: If a game is being broadcast nationally on ABC, ESPN, TNT, or NBA TV, it is blacked out on League Pass across the entire United States. The Solution: How VPNs Works A VPN routes your internet connection through a server in a location of your choosing. It masks your real IP address and assigns you a new one from that server's location. If you live in Los Angeles and the Lakers are blacked out locally, you can use ExpressVPN to connect to a server in Chicago. As far as NBA League Pass is concerned, you are currently sitting in Illinois, meaning the Los Angeles local blackout no longer applies to you. Why ExpressVPN? When streaming live sports, your VPN needs to be fast and reliable. A dropped connection or heavy buffering in the final two minutes of a tied game is unacceptable. ExpressVPN is the premier choice for NBA streaming for a few key reasons: Blazing Fast Speeds: ExpressVPN consistently ranks as one of the fastest VPNs available, minimizing the risk of buffering or quality drops during a live broadcast. Massive Server Network: They have servers in numerous cities across the United States. If one region is blacked out, you have plenty of other domestic options to choose from. Device Compatibility: ExpressVPN has dedicated, easy-to-use apps for Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, and even routers and smart TVs, meaning you can watch the game on your preferred screen. Reliable Bypassing: They frequently update their server IP addresses, making it difficult for streaming services to detect and block the VPN traffic. Step-by-Step Guide: How to Watch Blacked-Out NBA Games Ready to bypass the restrictions? Follow these steps to get your game on the screen. Step 1: Sign up and Install ExpressVPN Head to the ExpressVPN website and choose a subscription plan. Once you have created your account, download and install the ExpressVPN app on the device you plan to use for streaming (e.g., your laptop, smartphone, or tablet). Step 2: Clear Your Browser Cache or App Data Crucial Step: Before turning on the VPN, make sure NBA League Pass doesn't remember your real location from a previous session. If on a computer: Clear your browser's cookies and cache. If on a mobile device: Force close the NBA app and clear its cache in your device settings. Step 3: Connect to an Out-of-Market Server Open the ExpressVPN app. Click the location selector (usually a three-dot menu next to the current location) and search for a United States server that is outside the blackout zone. Example: If the Knicks are playing the Celtics, do not connect to servers in New York or Boston. Connect to a server in Dallas or Miami instead. Verification: Once you click connect, the ExpressVPN shield will turn green, indicating your connection is secure and your location has been virtually changed. Step 4: Log into NBA League Pass Now that your ExpressVPN connection is active, navigate to the NBA website or open the NBA app and log into your League Pass account. Step 5: Stream the Game Select the game you want to watch. Because your IP address now shows you are in an out-of-market city, the blackout restriction will be bypassed, and the live stream will begin playing immediately. Troubleshooting Pro-Tips If you followed the steps above and are still seeing a blackout message, try these quick fixes: Switch Servers: Occasionally, a streaming service might flag a specific VPN server IP. Simply disconnect ExpressVPN, choose a different U.S. city from the server list, reconnect, and refresh your browser. Use Incognito Mode: If you are watching on a computer, try opening an Incognito or Private Browsing window after connecting to ExpressVPN. This ensures no lingering location data is leaking through your browser history. Turn off GPS: If you are using a mobile device, League Pass may check your phone's physical GPS location in addition to your IP address. While VPNs change your IP, they don't spoof GPS on all devices. You may have better luck streaming via a desktop or laptop browser if mobile is giving you trouble. With ExpressVPN in your rotation, you can stop staring at blackout screens and get back to enjoying the NBA season the way it was meant to be watched-without restrictions.

items.title: Victor Wembanyama Sets Survey Record As NBA GMs' Top Choice To Start Franchise
items.summary: Victor Wembanyama received 93% of the votes as the player NBA general managers would most want to start a franchise with. That was up from 83% a year ago. The San Antonio Spurs star led eight categories in the 25th annual NBA GM Survey. Wembanyama's 93% set a record for the highest share in the survey's history. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander of the Oklahoma City Thunder and Cooper Flagg of the Dallas Mavericks also received votes. GMs also see Wembanyama as the favorite for MVP as he received 77% of the votes, also a survey record. Nikola Jokic of the Denver Nuggets was second at 10%, and Minnesota's Anthony Edwards was third at 7%. Gilgeous-Alexander and Boston's Jayson Tatum also received votes. Last year, 67% of GMs picked Jokic to win MVP. Wembanyama, 22, dominated the defensive categories. He received 97% of the votes for both best defensive player and best interior defender. He also topped the lists for most versatile player and the player who forces the most coaching adjustments. Jokic still led Wembanyama in two head-to-head categories. GMs voted Jokic the best center, 63% to 37%, and the best international player, 53% to 47%. Past GM picks for the player to start a franchise with: 2002-03: Shaquille O'Neal, 64% 2003-04: Tim Duncan, 57% 2004-05: Tim Duncan, 48% 2005-06: Tim Duncan, 40% 2006-07: LeBron James, 71% 2007-08: LeBron James, 59% 2008-09: LeBron James, 67% 2009-10: LeBron James, 79% 2010-11: Kevin Durant, 56% 2011-12: Kevin Durant and LeBron James (tie), 37% 2012-13: LeBron James, 80% 2013-14: LeBron James, 90% 2014-15: LeBron James, 50% 2015-16: Anthony Davis, 86% 2016-17: Karl-Anthony Towns, 48% 2017-18: Karl-Anthony Towns, 29% 2018-19: Giannis Antetokounmpo, 30% 2019-20: Giannis Antetokounmpo, 86% 2020-21: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Luka Doncic (tie), 43% 2021-22: Luka Doncic, 43% 2022-23: Giannis Antetokounmpo, 55% 2023-24: Nikola Jokic, 33% 2024-25: Victor Wembanyama, 77% 2025-26: Victor Wembanyama, 83% 2026-27: Victor Wembanyama, 93%

items.title: 93 Percent Of NBA GMs Pick Spurs Or Thunder To Win 2027 NBA Championship
items.summary: NBA general managers overwhelmingly predict the 2027 champion to come from the Western Conference. In the 25th annual NBA GM Survey, 93 percent picked either the San Antonio Spurs or the Oklahoma City Thunder to win the title. San Antonio received 50% of the votes and Oklahoma City got 43%. The New York Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers also received votes. GMs could not vote for their own teams. A year ago, 80% of GMs picked the Thunder to win the championship, and the Knicks won it instead when they defeated the Spurs. Oklahoma City was eliminated by the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals in seven games. The Spurs and Thunder are also close in the West rankings. San Antonio received 53% of first-place votes to Oklahoma City's 47%, and both teams finished with 34% of the total points. Last year, 87% picked the Thunder to win the West. The Knicks are the clear favorite in the East, with 60% of first-place votes. The 76ers were second at 23%. Last year, 63% of GMs picked the Cleveland Cavaliers to win the East. San Antonio also led in other categories. The Spurs received 87% of votes for the most promising young core. Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper are 22, 21 and 20 years old. The Thunder are at +250 to win the NBA Championship, while the Spurs are at +280, according to the latest basketball betting odds . items.title: Tim Connelly Unconcerned About Job Security As Timberwolves Keep Taking 'Big Swings'
items.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves president Tim Connelly says the risk of being fired won't stop him from making bold moves. Connelly is entering the final season of his contract and has reshaped the roster every year since 2022. "If it doesn't work and it's my job, I'll get fired," said Connelly. "That's fine. But I don't ever want to be in a position where we're reluctant to take big swings." Connelly has turned down other opportunities and said his family is happy in Minnesota. Connelly made more big changes this summer after a second-round loss to the San Antonio Spurs. Minnesota traded Julius Randle and Naz Reid, acquired LaMelo Ball and signed Jonathan Kuminga. "My industry has become so risk-averse," said Connelly. "They're so concerned about real-time analysis (from the media). ... In all reality, either you're trying to win, or you're chasing that." Connelly has made at least one major deal every season since leaving the Denver Nuggets. Six weeks into the job, he traded five players, four first-round picks and a pick swap for Rudy Gobert. In 2024, Connelly sent Karl-Anthony Towns to the New York Knicks for Randle, Donte DiVincenzo and a first-round pick. Last February, Connelly traded Rob Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in 2024, to the Chicago Bulls for Ayo Dosunmu. Over four years, Connelly's major trades have used six first-round picks, five first-round swaps and seven second-round picks. Minnesota has made the playoffs in each of Connelly's four seasons and won at least one series in each of the last three. The Wolves lost in five games in the Western Conference finals in both 2024 and 2025. Anthony Edwards, 25, has played with a different supporting cast in each of the past three seasons. "It means a lot," said Edwards. "We've had, what, three different teams going into three different years. So hopefully we can settle in with this squad."
